The [opening page](../../index.qmd#cases) sets the four cases side by side. The case study of each, [the housing-audit case](../../cases/housing/index.qmd), [the immigration-and-trust case](../../cases/trust/index.qmd), [the cohabitation case](../../cases/cohabitation/index.qmd) and [the EU-frames case](../../cases/eu-frames/index.qmd), is the place to start when the term reaches it.

This track spreads the course over a term of twelve weekly sessions and takes its exercise through all four cases, in the order of their difficulty: the housing-audit case, the immigration-and-trust case, the cohabitation case and the EU-frames case. It suits a class of students of sociology, politics or demography who meet once a week for about two hours and can give three to four hours more to the course on their own, with time to read the four papers and to fetch the data that the last case builds on. No programming is assumed, and the first two weeks set up R, an IDE and Quarto before any case begins.

Every case runs through the same five tasks. Task 1 is the setup check; Task 2 meets the data, writes the estimand statement and finishes the causal graph; Task 3 reproduces a result that Multi100 recorded for one of five analysts; Task 4 explores the specification menu one decision at a time; and Task 5 declares one specification in a short preregistration, runs it and reports it. The tasks therefore come round four times, and each case asks more of the statistics and of the data handling than the one before it, from a comparison of proportions among a thousand emails to panel models fitted to country-years that you build yourself from sixteen surveys. The later cases move faster through what the earlier ones taught and spend the time saved on what is new.

Each week has a page with a table of what to work through, and every row links a page or a section that already exists on this site. A figure in the Timing column is the whole of the work that the row asks for, and the rows of a week add up to between five and six hours. About two of those hours are the class meeting, which takes the rows of slides and most of the tasks, so that the class can compare its numbers as they arrive. The other three to four hours, the papers, the case studies and the companion modules, are your own work between meetings. The data that the tasks need ship with the workspace of each case, apart from the file of Task 3 of the immigration-and-trust case, which the workspace downloads for you. In week 10 you also download the sixteen Eurobarometer files from which the panel of the EU-frames case was built, which needs a free account at GESIS: open it in week 9 at the latest.

| | Case | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| [Week 1 – Credibility and the three Rs](week-1.qmd) | – | Why the field talks of a crisis, reproduction, robustness and replication, SCORE and Multi100, and R, Quarto and an IDE installed. |
| [Week 2 – R and Quarto](week-2.qmd) | Housing audit | A first session in R on the data of a field experiment, the document format of the reports, and the first paper. |
| [Week 3 – The claim and its reproduction](week-3.qmd) | Housing audit | Tasks 1 to 3: the estimand statement, the graph of an experiment, and a recorded $\chi^2$ reproduced from the public file. |
| [Week 4 – The menu and the declaration](week-4.qmd) | Housing audit | Tasks 4 and 5, randomisation inference and power, the replication with new data, and the first case report. |
| [Week 5 – Survey data and scales](week-5.qmd) | Immigration and trust | Tasks 1 and 2 on the European Social Survey: an attitude scale and its reliability, and what the controls of the paper are. |
| [Week 6 – Regression on respondents](week-6.qmd) | Immigration and trust | Task 3: a multilevel model reproduced, fixed effects against random intercepts, survey weights, and errors clustered by 16 countries. |
| [Week 7 – The menu and the public record](week-7.qmd) | Immigration and trust | Tasks 4 and 5, two rebuilds of the data that part ways, the file of the analysts, how a record keeps its versions, and the second case report. |
| [Week 8 – Unions as person-months](week-8.qmd) | Cohabitation | Tasks 1 and 2 on the National Survey of Family Growth: censoring, the life table, and a comparison made among women who all cohabited. |
| [Week 9 – The reproduction and competing risks](week-9.qmd) | Cohabitation | Tasks 3 to 5: a recorded test reproduced and what it rests on, discrete-time models with two ways out of a union, and the third case report. |
| [Week 10 – From respondents to a panel](week-10.qmd) | EU frames | Tasks 1 to 3: sixteen Eurobarometer files turned into country-years, panel fixed and random effects, and a recorded *t* reproduced. |
| [Week 11 – Few clusters and the multiverse](week-11.qmd) | EU frames | Tasks 4 and 5 on a curve of 864 specifications, inference with 27 countries, missing answers, the fourth case report, and the preregistration of the final project. |
| [Week 12 – The final project](week-12.qmd) | Your choice | A question beyond the claim of one case, declared before it runs, versioned with git and ready to archive. |

Each case takes one claim of a published article, by an original author or authors whom the pages of the case call the OA or the OAs, and the term asks you to read all four articles, each in the week in which its case begins: the field experiment on public housing authorities in the United States [@EinsteinGlick2017DoesRaceAffect] in week 2, the survey study of concern about immigration and trust in politics in Western Europe [@McLaren2012CulturalDivideEurope] in week 5, the study of cohabiting unions and marriage among American women [@KuoRaley2016DivergingPatternsUnion] in week 8, and the study of economic crisis and how citizens frame the European Union [@Teney2016DoesEUEconomic] in week 10.

By the end of the term you hold four case reports. Each contains the estimand statement and the causal graph of its claim, the reproduction of a recorded result, your exploration of the menu, a preregistration completed before its specification ran, and the result of that specification with its place on the curve of the claim. You also hold a final project that asks a question beyond the claim of one case, preregistered before it ran. All five sit in a version-controlled repository that another person can clone and re-render, with the licensed survey files left out of it, as the terms of their archive require.

For a term on one case alone, the [semester track of the EU-frames case](../eu-frames-semester/index.qmd) spends ten sessions on that case and the companion modules that it uses.
